CONSTANTS
  Students = {stuAda, stuBen}
  Sections = {sec101, sec202}
  MaxCycle = 2
  NoStudent = nostudent
  NoSection = nosection

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleHolder
nl:
A university course-registration system gates every action on advising clearance rather than on who a student is. The registrar runs an advising cycle, and each student carries the cycle number their clearance was issued under; clearance carried from a closed cycle is worthless. Registration is arranged in two levels: a single registration desk that must be taken first, and a per-section hold that is taken second. Students are slow but never disappear, so the registrar waits for the desk and every section hold to be given back rather than forcing them open.

The registrar may roll the advising cycle only while the desk is free and no section is held. A student whose clearance is out of date, and who is holding neither the desk nor a section, may be re-advised, taking the current cycle onto their clearance. A student carrying current clearance and not already registered may take the free desk, and a student at the desk may step away from it. A student at the desk carrying current clearance may take a hold on any free section, which releases the desk in the same step. A student holding a section, still carrying current clearance and not already registered, may register into that section, which releases the hold. A student holding a section may also give the hold back without registering. A registered student may withdraw, freeing their registration.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whoever is standing at the registration desk, and whoever is holding a section open, is carrying clearance issued under the advising cycle the registrar is currently running.

---- MODULE W4Od7m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Cans, Quorum, NoCan

VARIABLES ballot, up, cleared, bench, manifest

vars == <<ballot, up, cleared, bench, manifest>>

NumCans == Cardinality(Cans)

Alive == {k \in Controllers : up[k]}

Struck(c) == \E i \in 1..Len(manifest) : manifest[i] = c

\* Breaking a customs seal cannot be undone, so it takes a quorum of yard
\* controllers before a can even reaches the bench. Controllers can go quiet
\* without warning; the quorum is sized so one going quiet is survivable.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ballot \in [Cans -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ up \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ cleared \in [Cans -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ bench \in Cans \cup {NoCan}
  /\ manifest \in Seq(Cans)

Init ==
  /\ ballot = [c \in Cans |-> {}]
  /\ up = [k \in Controllers |-> TRUE]
  /\ cleared = [c \in Cans |-> FALSE]
  /\ bench = NoCan
  /\ manifest = << >>

Paperwork(c) ==
  /\ ~cleared[c]
  /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, up, bench, manifest>>

Endorse(k, c) ==
  /\ up[k]
  /\ ~Struck(c)
  /\ k \notin ballot[c]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, cleared, bench, manifest>>

GoQuiet(k) ==
  /\ up[k]
  /\ Cardinality(Alive) > Quorum
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, cleared, bench, manifest>>

\* A can only reaches the bench once, and only with the ballot behind it.
Stage(c) ==
  /\ bench = NoCan
  /\ cleared[c]
  /\ ~Struck(c)
  /\ Cardinality(ballot[c]) >= Quorum
  /\ bench' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, up, cleared, manifest>>

Strike ==
  /\ bench # NoCan
  /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, bench)
  /\ bench' = NoCan
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, up, cleared>>

Handover ==
  /\ Len(manifest) = NumCans
  /\ manifest' = << >>
  /\ ballot' = [c \in Cans |-> {}]
  /\ cleared' = [c \in Cans |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, bench>>

Filing == \E c \in Cans : Paperwork(c)
Endorsing == \E k \in Controllers, c \in Cans : Endorse(k, c)
Staging == \E c \in Cans : Stage(c)

Next ==
  \/ Filing
  \/ Endorsing
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : GoQuiet(k)
  \/ Staging
  \/ Strike
  \/ Handover

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Filing)
  /\ WF_vars(Endorsing)
  /\ WF_vars(Staging)
  /\ WF_vars(Strike)

\* Intent: the seal log never names the same can twice. A can whose seal has
\* already been broken must never come back round for a second strike.
ManifestHasNoRepeat ==
  \A i, j \in 1..Len(manifest) : manifest[i] = manifest[j] => i = j

ShiftCompletes == <>(Len(manifest) = NumCans)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {ctlA, ctlB, ctlC}
  Cans = {canP, canQ}
  Quorum = 2
  NoCan = nocan

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ManifestHasNoRepeat

PROPERTY ShiftCompletes
nl:
A container-ship crane yard breaks customs seals on cans before they are released inland. Breaking a seal cannot be undone, so no can reaches the cutting bench until a quorum of yard controllers has endorsed it. Controllers can go quiet without warning and give no sign of having done so; the quorum is sized so that one controller going quiet is survivable. Every seal that is broken is written into the shift's seal log, in the order the strikes happened.

Paperwork may be filed for any can that has not been cleared yet. A controller that is still up may endorse any can whose seal has not already been struck, once each. A controller that is up may go quiet, but only while more controllers are up than the quorum needs. A can may be staged onto the cutting bench when the bench is empty, the can is cleared, its seal has not already been struck, and its ballot has reached the quorum. The can on the bench is struck: its seal is broken, the can is written into the seal log, and the bench empties. When the log holds every can, the shift hands over: the log is emptied and the ballots and paperwork are reset for the next shift. The yard keeps moving -- paperwork is always eventually filed, endorsements are always eventually given, a qualified can is always eventually staged, and a staged can is always eventually struck.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The seal log never names the same can twice, so no can's seal is ever broken more than once in a shift.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every shift eventually reaches the point where the seal log holds every can.

---- MODULE W4Od13m2p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Routes, Purse, NoRoute

VARIABLES till, escrow, vault, phase, claim

vars == <<till, escrow, vault, phase, claim>>

RECURSIVE Pot(_, _)
Pot(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Pot(f, S \ {x})

Mine(r) == {m \in Machines : claim[m] = r}

\* Two route operators run their own collection rounds against one shared
\* coin vault. A round is two-phase: coin moved into escrow has left the till
\* but not yet reached the vault, and it is counted the whole time.

TypeOK ==
  /\ till \in [Machines -> 0..Purse]
  /\ escrow \in [Machines -> 0..Purse]
  /\ vault \in 0..Purse
  /\ phase \in [Routes -> {"idle", "prep", "commit", "abort"}]
  /\ claim \in [Machines -> Routes \cup {NoRoute}]

Init ==
  /\ till = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ escrow = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ vault = Purse
  /\ phase = [r \in Routes |-> "idle"]
  /\ claim = [m \in Machines |-> NoRoute]

Open(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "idle"
  /\ Mine(r) = {}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "prep"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, escrow, vault, claim>>

Enlist(r, m) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "prep"
  /\ claim[m] = NoRoute
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![m] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, escrow, vault, phase>>

Prepare(r, m, n) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "prep"
  /\ claim[m] = r
  /\ escrow[m] = 0
  /\ till[m] >= n
  /\ till' = [till EXCEPT ![m] = @ - n]
  /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![m] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, phase, claim>>

\* Commit sweeps escrow into the vault; the coin is not created there, it
\* just stops being counted at the machine.
Commit(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "prep"
  /\ Mine(r) # {}
  /\ \A m \in Mine(r) : escrow[m] > 0
  /\ vault' = vault + Pot([m \in Machines |->
                             IF claim[m] = r THEN escrow[m] ELSE 0], Machines)
  /\ escrow' = [m \in Machines |-> IF claim[m] = r THEN 0 ELSE escrow[m]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "commit"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, claim>>

Abort(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "prep"
  /\ till' = [m \in Machines |->
                IF claim[m] = r THEN till[m] + escrow[m] ELSE till[m]]
  /\ escrow' = [m \in Machines |-> IF claim[m] = r THEN 0 ELSE escrow[m]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "abort"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, claim>>

Close(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] \in {"commit", "abort"}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ claim' = [m \in Machines |-> IF claim[m] = r THEN NoRoute ELSE claim[m]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, escrow, vault>>

Refill(m) ==
  /\ vault > 0
  /\ till[m] < Purse
  /\ vault' = vault - 1
  /\ till' = [till EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<escrow, phase, claim>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Routes : Open(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routes, m \in Machines : Enlist(r, m)
  \/ \E r \in Routes, m \in Machines, n \in 1..Purse : Prepare(r, m, n)
  \/ \E r \in Routes : Commit(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routes : Abort(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routes : Close(r)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Refill(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Intent: coin is only ever moved, never made or lost. Tills, escrow and
\* the shared vault always add back up to the float the network started with.
CoinConserved ==
  Pot(till, Machines) + Pot(escrow, Machines) + vault = Purse

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {mchLobby, mchDepot}
  Routes = {routeNorth, routeSouth}
  Purse = 3
  NoRoute = noroute

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CoinConserved
nl:
A vending machine network is worked by two independent route operators that run their own collection rounds against one shared coin vault. A collection round is a two-phase commit across the machines the operator has enlisted: coin moved into escrow has left a machine's till but has not yet reached the vault, and it is counted the whole time it is in flight. The network's coin float never changes size; coin only ever moves between a till, an escrow, and the vault.

An idle operator holding no machines may open a round. An operator in the prepare phase may enlist any machine that no operator holds. An operator may prepare a machine it holds whose escrow is empty, moving an amount out of that machine's till into that machine's escrow, provided the till holds that much. An operator in the prepare phase holding at least one machine, with every machine it holds having something in escrow, may commit: the escrow of all its machines is swept into the shared vault and those escrows are emptied. An operator in the prepare phase may instead abort, which puts each held machine's escrow back into that same machine's till. After committing or aborting the operator closes the round, going idle and releasing every machine it held. Separately, a coin may be taken from the vault and refilled into any machine's till that has room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The coin sitting in all machine tills, plus the coin sitting in all escrows, plus the coin in the shared vault, always equals the float the network started with.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trackers, Matches, MaxTerm, NoNode

VARIABLES store, lead, term, acked, pend

vars == <<store, lead, term, acked, pend>>

\* The cross-match register is primary-copy replicated: followers take the
\* primary's copy wholesale, so a primary elected behind the acknowledged
\* frontier would quietly erase confirmed cross-matches. The vote guard is
\* what stops that. Trackers lag but never die.

TypeOK ==
  /\ store \in [Trackers -> SUBSET Matches]
  /\ lead \in Trackers \cup {NoNode}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ acked \subseteq Matches
  /\ pend \subseteq Matches

Init ==
  /\ store = [n \in Trackers |-> {}]
  /\ lead = NoNode
  /\ term = 0
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ pend = {}

Raise(x) ==
  /\ x \notin pend
  /\ \A n \in Trackers : x \notin store[n]
  /\ pend' = pend \cup {x}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<store, lead, term, acked>>

Apply(x) ==
  /\ lead # NoNode
  /\ x \in pend
  /\ x \notin store[lead]
  /\ store' = [store EXCEPT ![lead] = @ \cup {x}]
  /\ pend' = pend \ {x}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, term, acked>>

\* A follower takes the primary's copy as it stands, additions and gaps alike.
Adopt(n) ==
  /\ lead # NoNode
  /\ n # lead
  /\ store' = [store EXCEPT ![n] = store[lead]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, term, acked, pend>>

Confirm(x) ==
  /\ lead # NoNode
  /\ \A n \in Trackers : x \in store[n]
  /\ x \notin acked
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {x}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<store, lead, term, pend>>

\* Only a tracker that already carries every acknowledged cross-match may
\* take the primary post.
Elect(n) ==
  /\ lead = NoNode
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ acked \subseteq store[n]
  /\ lead' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<store, acked, pend>>

Stand(n) ==
  /\ lead = n
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ lead' = NoNode
  /\ UNCHANGED <<store, term, acked, pend>>

Raising == \E x \in Matches : Raise(x)
Applying == \E x \in Matches : Apply(x)
Adopting == \E n \in Trackers : Adopt(n)
Confirming == \E x \in Matches : Confirm(x)
Electing == \E n \in Trackers : Elect(n)

Next ==
  \/ Raising
  \/ Applying
  \/ Adopting
  \/ Confirming
  \/ Electing
  \/ \E n \in Trackers : Stand(n)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Raising)
  /\ WF_vars(Applying)
  /\ WF_vars(Adopting)
  /\ WF_vars(Confirming)
  /\ WF_vars(Electing)

\* Intent: once a cross-match has been confirmed to the ward it is on every
\* tracker's copy and stays there, whatever happens to the primary post.
NoConfirmedMatchLost ==
  \A n \in Trackers : acked \subseteq store[n]

RegisterCatchesUp == <>(acked = Matches)

====

CONSTANTS
  Trackers = {trkAlpha, trkBeta}
  Matches = {xmatchU1, xmatchU2}
  MaxTerm = 2
  NoNode = nonode

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoConfirmedMatchLost

PROPERTY RegisterCatchesUp
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps a cross-match register replicated across a small set of tracker nodes, with one node acting as primary for the current term. Replication is primary-copy: a follower takes the primary's copy wholesale, gaps included, rather than merging. Trackers can lag arbitrarily but never die outright, so a lagging follower always catches up eventually. A cross-match is only confirmed back to the ward once every tracker is carrying it.

A cross-match that is not already pending and is not on any tracker's copy may be raised onto the pending list. The primary may apply a pending cross-match to its own copy, taking it off the pending list. A follower may adopt the primary's copy exactly as it stands. A cross-match that every tracker carries and that has not yet been confirmed may be confirmed to the ward. While terms remain, the primary post may be filled by any tracker that already carries every confirmed cross-match; taking the post advances the term. The sitting primary may stand down while terms remain, leaving the post vacant. Work never stops: raises, applies, adoptions, confirmations and elections all happen eventually whenever they are possible.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every cross-match that has been confirmed to the ward is present on every tracker's copy at all times, so no confirmed update is ever erased by a change of primary.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The register eventually reaches the point where every cross-match has been confirmed to the ward.

---- MODULE W4Od4m4p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, Intake, MaxLanes, NoCar

VARIABLES rank, line, bay, sealed, lanes

vars == <<rank, line, bay, sealed, lanes>>

\* The hot-wax bay is the one step that cannot be taken back. The holding
\* rank in front of the conveyor is bounded, and the number of conveyor
\* lanes actually running is changed by the operator while cars are on it.

OnRank(c) == \E i \in 1..Len(rank) : rank[i] = c
OnLine(c) == \E i \in 1..Len(line) : line[i] = c

TypeOK ==
  /\ rank \in Seq(Cars)
  /\ line \in Seq(Cars)
  /\ bay \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
  /\ sealed \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ lanes \in 1..MaxLanes

Init ==
  /\ rank = << >>
  /\ line = << >>
  /\ bay = NoCar
  /\ sealed = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
  /\ lanes = 1

\* A full holding rank simply turns cars away; that is the whole backpressure
\* story at the front gate.
Arrive(c) ==
  /\ Len(rank) < Intake
  /\ ~sealed[c]
  /\ ~OnRank(c)
  /\ ~OnLine(c)
  /\ bay # c
  /\ rank' = Append(rank, c)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<line, bay, sealed, lanes>>

Load ==
  /\ rank # << >>
  /\ Len(line) < lanes
  /\ line' = Append(line, Head(rank))
  /\ rank' = Tail(rank)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bay, sealed, lanes>>

Advance ==
  /\ line # << >>
  /\ bay = NoCar
  /\ ~sealed[Head(line)]
  /\ bay' = Head(line)
  /\ line' = Tail(line)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rank, sealed, lanes>>

Wax ==
  /\ bay # NoCar
  /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![bay] = TRUE]
  /\ bay' = NoCar
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rank, line, lanes>>

Bypass ==
  /\ line # << >>
  /\ sealed[Head(line)]
  /\ line' = Tail(line)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rank, bay, sealed, lanes>>

\* Lanes are taken out and put back while the line is running; the operator
\* may not cut below what is already on the belt.
Retune ==
  /\ lanes' \in (1..MaxLanes) \ {lanes}
  /\ Len(line) =< lanes'
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rank, line, bay, sealed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c)
  \/ Load
  \/ Advance
  \/ Wax
  \/ Bypass
  \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Intent: a car standing in the hot-wax bay has never been waxed. Since the
\* bay is the only way the coat gets applied, no car is ever coated twice.
NeverWaxedTwice ==
  bay # NoCar => ~sealed[bay]

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {carPlum, carSlate}
  Intake = 2
  MaxLanes = 2
  NoCar = nocar

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NeverWaxedTwice
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line pulls cars from a bounded holding rank onto a conveyor and past a hot-wax bay. Applying the hot-wax coat is the one step that cannot be taken back: once a car is coated it stays coated. The holding rank has a fixed depth, and when it is full the front gate simply turns cars away -- that is the whole backpressure story. The number of conveyor lanes actually running is changed by the operator while cars are on the belt.

A car that has not been coated, and that is not already on the rank, on the conveyor, or in the wax bay, may arrive onto the rank while the rank is below its depth. The car at the head of the rank may be loaded onto the conveyor while the conveyor holds fewer cars than there are lanes running. The car at the head of the conveyor may advance into the wax bay when the bay is empty and that car has not been coated. The car in the bay is waxed: it takes the coat and leaves the bay. A car at the head of the conveyor that already carries the coat bypasses the bay and rolls off the end of the line. The operator may retune the number of running lanes to any other permitted value, but may not cut below the number of cars already on the belt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car standing in the hot-wax bay has not been coated before, so no car ever receives the hot-wax coat twice.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m0p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Routers, Bags, Flights, MaxVer, NoSnap

VARIABLES ver, snap, bill, duty

vars == <<ver, snap, bill, duty>>

Card == [bag : Bags, v : 0..MaxVer]

Placed(b) == \E f \in Flights : bill[f][b]

\* Routers work optimistically: read the routing card, then write only if the
\* card's version has not moved underneath them. Putting a bag in a can is
\* the point of no return, so the version bump on that write is what makes a
\* second router's stale card fail instead of loading the bag again.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [Bags -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ snap \in [Routers -> Card \cup {NoSnap}]
  /\ bill \in [Flights -> [Bags -> BOOLEAN]]
  /\ duty \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ ver = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
  /\ snap = [r \in Routers |-> NoSnap]
  /\ bill = [f \in Flights |-> [b \in Bags |-> FALSE]]
  /\ duty = FALSE

Read(r, b) ==
  /\ snap[r] = NoSnap
  /\ ~Placed(b)
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = [bag |-> b, v |-> ver[b]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, bill, duty>>

Load(r, f) ==
  /\ snap[r] # NoSnap
  /\ ver[snap[r].bag] = snap[r].v
  /\ ver[snap[r].bag] < MaxVer
  /\ bill' = [bill EXCEPT ![f][snap[r].bag] = TRUE]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snap[r].bag] = @ + 1]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED duty

Retry(r) ==
  /\ snap[r] # NoSnap
  /\ ver[snap[r].bag] # snap[r].v
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, bill, duty>>

Retag(b) ==
  /\ ver[b] < MaxVer - 1
  /\ ~Placed(b)
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, bill, duty>>

Arm ==
  /\ ~duty
  /\ duty' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, bill>>

Stand ==
  /\ duty
  /\ duty' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, bill>>

\* The duty manager can put a bag on a can with no card read at all, but the
\* bump still happens, so any router holding that card is thrown back.
Force(f, b) ==
  /\ duty
  /\ ~Placed(b)
  /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
  /\ bill' = [bill EXCEPT ![f][b] = TRUE]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, duty>>

Reading == \E r \in Routers, b \in Bags : Read(r, b)
Loading == \E r \in Routers, f \in Flights : Load(r, f)
Retrying == \E r \in Routers : Retry(r)

Next ==
  \/ Reading
  \/ Loading
  \/ Retrying
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Retag(b)
  \/ Arm
  \/ Stand
  \/ \E f \in Flights, b \in Bags : Force(f, b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Reading)
  /\ WF_vars(Loading)
  /\ WF_vars(Retrying)

\* Intent: a bag appears on the load bill of one aircraft at most. Two bills
\* naming the same bag would mean the point of no return was passed twice.
BagLoadedOnce ==
  \A b \in Bags : \A f, g \in Flights :
    (bill[f][b] /\ bill[g][b]) => f = g

EveryBagPlaced == <>(\A b \in Bags : Placed(b))

====
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to aircraft load cans. Each bag has a routing card carrying a version number, and routers work optimistically: a router reads a bag's card, and later writes only if that card's version has not moved underneath it. Putting a bag into a can is the point of no return -- once a bag is on a flight's load bill it stays there -- so the write bumps the version, which is exactly what makes a second router's stale card fail instead of loading the bag again. The duty manager also has a privileged override.

A router with no card in hand may read the card of any bag that is not yet on any load bill. A router holding a card may load its bag onto any flight, but only if the bag's live version still equals the version on the card it is holding; loading writes the bag onto that flight's bill, bumps the bag's version, and hands the card back. A router holding a card whose version no longer matches the live version must retry, throwing the card away so it can read again. A bag that is not yet on a bill may be retagged, which bumps its version and invalidates any card read against it. The duty manager may come on station or stand down, and while on station may force a bag that is not yet on any bill straight onto a flight's bill with no card read at all; the forced write still bumps the version, so any router holding that bag's card is thrown back. Routers keep working: reads, loads and retries all happen eventually whenever they are possible.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No bag appears on the load bill of two different flights, so a bag is never committed to a can more than once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag eventually ends up on some flight's load bill.

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Orders, Slots, NoOrder, NoSlot

VARIABLES bus, arm, served, credit, tech

vars == <<bus, arm, served, credit, tech>>

\* Two levels of lock: the machine bus must be taken before any slot motor
\* can be armed, and the bus is handed straight back once a motor is armed.
\* Turning a motor drops product, which cannot be taken back.

Armed(o) == \E s \in Slots : arm[s] = o

TypeOK ==
  /\ bus \in Orders \cup {NoOrder}
  /\ arm \in [Slots -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]
  /\ served \in [Orders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ credit \in [Orders -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ tech \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ bus = NoOrder
  /\ arm = [s \in Slots |-> NoOrder]
  /\ served = [o \in Orders |-> NoSlot]
  /\ credit = [o \in Orders |-> FALSE]
  /\ tech = FALSE

Pay(o) ==
  /\ ~credit[o]
  /\ served[o] = NoSlot
  /\ credit' = [credit EXCEPT ![o] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, arm, served, tech>>

TakeBus(o) ==
  /\ bus = NoOrder
  /\ credit[o]
  /\ served[o] = NoSlot
  /\ ~Armed(o)
  /\ bus' = o
  /\ UNCHANGED <<arm, served, credit, tech>>

DropBus(o) ==
  /\ bus = o
  /\ bus' = NoOrder
  /\ UNCHANGED <<arm, served, credit, tech>>

\* Arming is the last point at which the order is checked against the drop
\* record; the bus goes back in the same step.
ArmSlot(o, s) ==
  /\ bus = o
  /\ arm[s] = NoOrder
  /\ served[o] = NoSlot
  /\ arm' = [arm EXCEPT ![s] = o]
  /\ bus' = NoOrder
  /\ UNCHANGED <<served, credit, tech>>

Turn(s) ==
  /\ arm[s] # NoOrder
  /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![arm[s]] = s]
  /\ credit' = [credit EXCEPT ![arm[s]] = FALSE]
  /\ arm' = [arm EXCEPT ![s] = NoOrder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, tech>>

Disarm(s) ==
  /\ arm[s] # NoOrder
  /\ arm' = [arm EXCEPT ![s] = NoOrder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, served, credit, tech>>

Callout ==
  /\ ~tech
  /\ tech' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, arm, served, credit>>

Signoff ==
  /\ tech
  /\ tech' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, arm, served, credit>>

\* The engineer's key turns a motor with no bus and no arming, but will not
\* touch an order that is already armed somewhere or already served.
KeyTurn(o, s) ==
  /\ tech
  /\ credit[o]
  /\ served[o] = NoSlot
  /\ ~Armed(o)
  /\ arm[s] = NoOrder
  /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![o] = s]
  /\ credit' = [credit EXCEPT ![o] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, arm, tech>>

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Pay(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : TakeBus(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : DropBus(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : ArmSlot(o, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Turn(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Disarm(s)
  \/ Callout
  \/ Signoff
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : KeyTurn(o, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Intent: a motor is only ever armed for an order that has had nothing
\* dropped for it yet. Since a drop is what writes the record, no order can
\* have product dropped for it twice.
ArmedOnlyForUnserved ==
  \A s \in Slots : arm[s] # NoOrder => served[arm[s]] = NoSlot

====

CONSTANTS
  Orders = {ordRed, ordBlue}
  Slots = {slotLeft, slotRight}
  NoOrder = noorder
  NoSlot = noslot

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ArmedOnlyForUnserved
nl:
A vending machine network fulfils paid orders through two levels of locking. There is one machine bus, which is the coarse lock, and each product slot has its own motor arming, which is the fine lock. Turning a slot motor drops product, and a drop cannot be taken back: the drop is written into the order's record and stays there. A service engineer also carries a key that bypasses the bus entirely.

An order that is unpaid and has had nothing dropped for it may be paid. A paid order with nothing dropped for it, and not currently armed at any slot, may take the machine bus when the bus is free; an order holding the bus may also hand it straight back. An order holding the bus may arm any slot whose motor is not already armed, provided nothing has been dropped for that order yet; arming hands the bus back in the same step. An armed slot may be turned: product drops, the drop is written into that order's record, the order's credit is spent, and the motor disarms. An armed slot may instead be disarmed without dropping, which is how a jam is cleared. The engineer may be called out and may sign off. While on site, the engineer's key turns any unarmed slot's motor for any paid order that has had nothing dropped for it and is not armed anywhere else, writing the drop and spending the credit with no bus and no arming.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot motor is only ever armed for an order that has had nothing dropped for it yet, so no order ever has product dropped for it twice.
